comparison: Both evaluations support the genome editing and validation claims (C2, C3, C23-C26). OpenEval emphasizes multiple independent clones and efficient differentiation, while peer reviewers confirm preserved physiology and state-of-the-art methodology. Both find the model development convincing.

Perfect agreement on TDP43 mislocalization and pathology (C28-C33). Both evaluations support the findings with OpenEval noting appropriate controls and quantification, while peer reviewers explicitly confirm nuclear depletion, cytosolic mislocalization, and aggregates without challenge.

Both support splicing defect findings (C34, C39, C40) with OpenEval emphasizing comprehensive multi-method validation and peer reviewers confirming cryptic exon induction as a hallmark of TDP-43 loss. OpenEval also covers long-read sequencing (C43-C46) which peer reviewers accept without challenge in R7.

Both support RT-qPCR validation of splicing events (C53-C54). OpenEval notes strong validation rate (12/12 for splicing), while peer reviewers acknowledge this as part of the comprehensive splicing analysis demonstrating functional TDP-43 loss.

Perfect agreement on transcriptomic changes (C35-C38). OpenEval details PCA variance and GO enrichment findings, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these RNAseq results as part of the convincing demonstration of functional TDP-43 depletion.

Both support concordance with patient data (C47-C49). OpenEval notes appropriate statistical analysis, while peer reviewers accept disease relevance without challenge. However, OpenEval also addresses mechanistic comparisons with knockdown (C50-C52) which peer reviewers question in R5.

Disagreement on interpretation of mislocalization vs knockdown differences (C50-C52). OpenEval supports the conclusion that differences suggest distinct mechanisms with appropriate caution. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, noting that different TDP-43 levels or batch effects could explain differences rather than mislocalization per se.

Both support the inducible model development (C55-C57). OpenEval emphasizes western blot controls showing phosphorylation changes, while peer reviewers explicitly praise the temporal control as a powerful feature lacking in current methods.

Both support stress granule analysis (C58-C60). OpenEval notes this distinguishes TDP43 puncta from stress granules, while peer reviewers accept this characterization as supporting model specificity without challenge.

Perfect agreement on temporal dynamics (C61-C63). OpenEval supports rapid onset of mislocalization and splicing defects as addressing key limitations, while peer reviewers accept these findings as demonstrating the model's value for studying early pathogenic events.

Both support splicing analysis in inducible model (C64-C65). OpenEval notes consistency with earlier results and appropriate statistical thresholds, while peer reviewers affirm the temporal control feature that enables this analysis.

Strong agreement on self-sustaining mislocalization (C66-C70). OpenEval finds this novel and important with appropriately cautious inferences, while peer reviewers implicitly acknowledge persistence as valuable for studying aggregate clearance pathways.

Both support microRNA dysregulation findings (C71-C73). OpenEval notes validation of known ALS-associated changes and bidirectional effects, while peer reviewers accept these findings as supporting disease relevance without challenge.

Disagreement on microRNA differences between mislocalization and knockdown (C74-C78). OpenEval supports the mechanistic inferences about distinct effects of nuclear loss versus cytoplasmic gain. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, citing concerns about TDP-43 levels and batch effects as alternative explanations.

Both support findings on TDP43 truncation absence (C79, C81-C82). OpenEval notes appropriate caution in acknowledging this model limitation, while peer reviewers accept the phosphorylation and truncation characterization without challenge.

Both support the overall summary claim (C4) that the model recapitulates TDP43 proteinopathy. OpenEval references multiple detailed experimental validations, while peer reviewers confirm the model convincingly demonstrates mislocalization and functional depletion with valuable research applications.

OpenEval evaluates background claims (C8-C22) as supported by citations, establishing scientific rationale and identifying limitations of existing models. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
OpenEval evaluates background claim C80 about truncated TDP43 isoforms as supported by citation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific background claim.

OpenEval rates future application claims (C83-C84) as uncertain, noting they represent reasonable but unvalidated speculation about future work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these forward-looking claims.
Peer reviewers also evaluate C27 (not in OpenEval R1) as part of model validation, though OpenEval includes C27 in its R1 evaluation of the same claim set.
